log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Empoleon
Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Rotom
Light Screen up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Lead Grimmsnarl+Empoleon: Grimmsnarl Fake Out (priority +3) flinches Whimsicott before Tailwind, and as Dark-type is immune to Whimsicott's Taunt/Encore. Empoleon resists Fairy/Ice and hits Whimsicott SE with Flash Cannon/Ice Beam. Rotom-Mow (Water resist, Thunderbolt/Leaf Storm 2x on Water mons) and Gengar (Shadow Ball 2x Gholdengo) back for cleanup.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Politoed Drizzle rain, Whimsicott Prankster (Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast, Focus Sash), Blastoise-Mega WaterSpout spread, Gholdengo Steel/Ghost MakeItRain/ShadowBall/Thunderbolt ChoiceScarf, Maushold FollowMe/Feint, Tauros-Aqua Intimidate/CloseCombat. Confirmed matchups: Moonblast 0.5x Empoleon (Steel); Shadow Ball 2x Gholdengo; Thunderbolt/Leaf Storm 2x Water types; WaterSpout 0.5x Rotom-Mow; Flash Cannon/Ice Beam 2x Whimsicott. Whimsicott Prankster status fails vs Dark (Grimmsnarl immune to Taunt/Encore). Plan: Grimmsnarl Fake Out shuts Tailwind turn 1; Empoleon frontline Fairy/Ice wall; Rotom-Mow pivot vs rain; Gengar Mega traps/disables Gholdengo/Whimsicott. Keep Slowbro Trick Room as backup if Tailwind dominates; Garchomp benched (STAB weak here, EQ hits ally).

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott and Blastoise to threaten immediate Mega Water Spout pressure while establishing Tailwind or denying Trick Room and disruption. Politoed preserves Drizzle and enables a second rain cycle; Scarf Gholdengo supplies strong spread damage and punishes Grimmsnarl and Psychic-based counterplay.
decisions.notebook: Core game plan: Whimsicott + Blastoise offers Tailwind, Prankster disruption, and Mega Water Spout pressure. Politoed preserves Drizzle for a later rain cycle and Helping Hand/Icy Wind support. Choice Scarf Gholdengo is the primary backline attacker and is especially valuable into Grimmsnarl and Psychic attackers. Maushold remains an alternative lead/support option when Follow Me is needed; Tauros-Aqua is the Intimidate and physical-pressure alternative.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out (+3) flinches Whimsicott through its Prankster Tailwind (+1), denying the speed control their rain/WaterSpout core needs. Empoleon Protects: attacking Blastoise only deals 13-19% (0.5x) while exposing it to Blastoise-Mega Aura Sphere 40-61% (2x SE). Protect keeps our Fairy/Ice wall healthy and scouts the unrevealed bench.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Politoed Drizzle rain, Whimsicott Prankster (Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast, Focus Sash), Blastoise-Mega WaterSpout spread + Aura Sphere (Mega Launcher 120, 2x into Empoleon Steel ~40-61%), Gholdengo Steel/Ghost MakeItRain/ShadowBall/Thunderbolt ChoiceScarf, Maushold FollowMe/Feint, Tauros-Aqua Intimidate/CloseCombat. Confirmed matchups: Moonblast 0.5x Empoleon; Shadow Ball 2x Gholdengo; Thunderbolt/Leaf Storm 2x Water; WaterSpout 0.5x Rotom-Mow; Flash Cannon/Ice Beam 2x Whimsicott; Aura Sphere 2x Empoleon. Damage facts: Empoleon Ice Beam 2x Whimsicott but Focus Sash saves at 1 HP; Ice Beam 0.5x Blastoise only 13-19%; Blastoise WaterSpout spread neutral into Grimmsnarl ~38-58%. Plan: Grimmsnarl Fake Out shuts Tailwind turn 1 (Prankster +1 loses to Fake Out +3); Empoleon frontline Fairy/Ice wall; Rotom-Mow pivot vs rain; Gengar Mega traps/disables Gholdengo/Whimsicott. Keep Slowbro Trick Room backup if Tailwind dominates; Garchomp benched (STAB weak here, EQ hits ally).

decisions.rationale: Switch Whimsicott to Gholdengo to deny Grimmsnarl’s likely Fake Out and preserve the Tailwind option. Mega Evolve Blastoise and use full-power spread Water Spout for immediate pressure on both foes; Aura Sphere is safer into Empoleon but gives up valuable board-wide damage.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Whimsicott for a later Tailwind or disruption turn, especially after Grimmsnarl is pressured or removed. Mega Blastoise is the preferred rain-mode attacker; Politoed should remain available to establish a later Drizzle cycle and provide Helping Hand or Icy Wind. Choice Scarf Gholdengo is valuable into Grimmsnarl and Psychic-oriented teams.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl at 27% would die to Gholdengo's Make It Rain (2x); switch to Gengar and Mega evolve for Shadow Tag to trap Gholdengo. Empoleon Ice Beam chips Gholdengo (0.5x). Preserve fragile Grimmsnarl, set up trap.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Politoed Drizzle rain, Whimsicott Prankster (Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast, Focus Sash), Blastoise-Mega WaterSpout spread + Aura Sphere (Mega Launcher, 2x into Empoleon ~40-61%), Gholdengo Steel/Ghost MakeItRain/ShadowBall/Thunderbolt ChoiceScarf, Maushold FollowMe/Feint, Tauros-Aqua Intimidate/CloseCombat. Matchups: Moonblast 0.5x Empoleon; Shadow Ball 2x Gholdengo (note: Ghost into Steel/Ghost may be 0.5x—verify); Thunderbolt/Leaf Storm 2x Water; WaterSpout 0.5x Rotom-Mow; Flash Cannon/Ice Beam 2x Whimsicott; Aura Sphere 2x Empoleon; Make It Rain 2x Grimmsnarl. Plan: Gengar Mega Shadow Tag traps Gholdengo/Whimsicott; Empoleon Fairy/Ice wall; Rotom-Mow pivot vs rain; Slowbro Trick Room backup; Garchomp benched (EQ hits ally).

decisions.rationale: Make It Rain guarantees the KO on weakened Grimmsnarl before it can establish screens or disrupt, while Aura Sphere pressures Empoleon with super-effective damage and may KO. This preserves both active attackers and avoids wasting Blastoise’s turn on a low-value spread Water Spout.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Whimsicott for a later Tailwind or disruption turn, especially after Grimmsnarl is pressured or removed. Mega Blastoise is the preferred rain-mode attacker; keep Politoed available to establish a later Drizzle cycle and provide Helping Hand or Icy Wind. Choice Scarf Gholdengo is valuable into Grimmsnarl and Psychic-oriented teams.

decisions.rationale: Gengar is guaranteed KO'd by Gholdengo's Choice-locked Make It Rain (32.8-46.7% > 15% HP) and cannot reliably KO Gholdengo (Shadow Ball 53.6-122.2%, speed tie uncertain). Switching Gengar to Rotom-Mow benches the fragile mon and brings a healthy Thunderbolt user (2x into Blastoise, possible OHKO). Empoleon protects to survive Blastoise's Aura Sphere (guaranteed KO from 23%); Make It Rain is only 3.7-5.6% into it.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Politoed Drizzle rain; Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast Focus Sash; Blastoise-Mega Mega Launcher Aura Sphere 2x Empoleon (KO from 23%), Water Spout spread, Ice Beam; Gholdengo Steel/Ghost ChoiceScarf locked Make It Rain (0.25x Empoleon, 1x others, Good as Gold blocks status); Maushold FollowMe/Feint FriendGuard; Tauros-Aqua Intimidate/CloseCombat. Plan: Gengar Mega Shadow Tag traps; Empoleon Fairy/Ice wall; Rotom-Mow Thunderbolt 2x Water; Grimmsnarl screens; Slowbro Trick Room backup; Garchomp benched.

decisions.rationale: Gholdengo is Choice-locked, and Make It Rain guarantees the KO on Gengar while also damaging Empoleon. Blastoise's Aura Sphere then guarantees the KO on Empoleon, clearing both active foes this turn.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Whimsicott for a later Tailwind or disruption turn, especially after Grimmsnarl is pressured or removed. Mega Blastoise is the preferred rain-mode attacker; keep Politoed available to establish a later Drizzle cycle and provide Helping Hand or Icy Wind. Choice Scarf Gholdengo remains valuable into Grimmsnarl and Psychic-oriented teams.

decisions.rationale: Rotom (138) outpaces Blastoise (98-130); Thunderbolt 2x near-guaranteed OHKO (68-147%, 102-219% crit). Blastoise acts before Empoleon and Aura Spheres Empoleon (32-55% > 47 HP) for the KO, so Empoleon can't help. It chips harmless Choice-locked Gholdengo with Steel-STAB Flash Cannon (12-27% vs Ice 9-20%); Gholdengo at -6 spa hits only 1-9%.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Politoed Drizzle rain; Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast Focus Sash; Blastoise-Mega Mega Launcher Aura Sphere 2x Empoleon, Water Spout spread, Ice Beam; Gholdengo Steel/Ghost ChoiceScarf locked Make It Rain (0.25x Empoleon, Good as Gold blocks status); Maushold FollowMe/Feint FriendGuard; Tauros-Aqua Intimidate/CloseCombat. Plan: Gengar Mega Shadow Tag traps; Empoleon Fairy/Ice wall; Rotom-Mow Thunderbolt 2x Water; Grimmsnarl screens; Slowbro Trick Room backup; Garchomp benched.

decisions.rationale: Don't forfeit—Blastoise-Mega is at 3% and we still field 3 Pokémon. Switch in Grimmsnarl: next turn its Fake Out flinches and KOs the 3% Blastoise-Mega (40BP Normal exceeds its remaining HP) and provides Prankster screens/Taunt. Gengar at 15% is too fragile (Ice Beam KOs) and less useful than Grimmsnarl's utility.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Politoed Drizzle rain; Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast Focus Sash; Blastoise-Mega Mega Launcher Aura Sphere/Water Spout/Ice Beam; Gholdengo Steel/Ghost ChoiceScarf Make It Rain (Good as Gold blocks status); Maushold FollowMe/Feint FriendGuard; Tauros-Aqua Intimidate/CloseCombat. Plan: Gengar Mega Shadow Tag traps; Empoleon Fairy/Ice wall; Rotom-Mow Thunderbolt 2x Water; Grimmsnarl Prankster screens + Fake Out on switch-in to flinch/KO low-HP foes; Slowbro Trick Room backup; Garchomp benched.

decisions.rationale: Switch Gholdengo to Politoed to preserve the valuable Scarf user and establish rain for a stronger Water Spout next turn. Blastoise uses Aura Sphere to guarantee the KO on Empoleon, removing its Protect/Surf pressure and improving the rain endgame.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Whimsicott for a later Tailwind or disruption turn, particularly once Grimmsnarl is pressured or removed. Mega Blastoise is the preferred rain-mode attacker; keep Politoed available to establish Drizzle cycles and provide Helping Hand or Icy Wind. Choice Scarf Gholdengo remains valuable into Grimmsnarl and Psychic-oriented teams.

decisions.rationale: Blastoise-Mega is at 3% HP. Grimmsnarl Prankster Taunt (+1 priority) lands before Blastoise acts, denying Protect; Rotom (faster, 138) then Thunderbolt in rain (1.5x) + SE 2x + Life Orb KOs it cleanly. Secures the kill and removes the Mega Launcher threat.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Politoed Drizzle rain; Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast Focus Sash; Blastoise-Mega Mega Launcher Aura Sphere/Water Spout/Ice Beam; Gholdengo Steel/Ghost ChoiceScarf Make It Rain (Good as Gold blocks status); Maushold FollowMe/Feint FriendGuard; Tauros-Aqua Intimidate/CloseCombat. Plan: Gengar Mega Shadow Tag traps; Empoleon Fairy/Ice wall; Rotom-Mow Thunderbolt 2x Water; Grimmsnarl Prankster screens + Fake Out on switch-in to flinch/KO low-HP foes; Slowbro Trick Room backup; Garchomp benched. Fake Out only works turn of switch-in (Grimmsnarl switched turn 4, so unavailable turn 5).

decisions.rationale: Blastoise must Protect because Rotom-Mow moves first and Thunderbolt otherwise KOs it. Politoed uses Icy Wind to damage both foes and lower Rotom-Mow's Speed, allowing Blastoise to move first next turn and finish it with Ice Beam while preserving the attacker.

Mega Blastoise is the preferred rain-mode attacker; keep Politoed available to re-establish Drizzle cycles and provide Helping Hand or Icy Wind. Choice Scarf Gholdengo remains valuable into Grimmsnarl and Psychic-oriented teams.

decisions.rationale: Blastoise-Mega sits at 3% and must be removed. Grimmsnarl's Prankster Taunt (priority +1) resolves before moves, blocking its Protect (already at reduced success), so Rotom's Thunderbolt (2x Electric, Life Orb) guarantees the KO and eliminates the Mega Launcher threat.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Politoed Drizzle rain; Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast Focus Sash; Blastoise-Mega Mega Launcher Aura Sphere/Water Spout/Ice Beam (Protect success reduced after turn 5 use); Gholdengo Steel/Ghost ChoiceScarf Make It Rain (Good as Gold blocks status); Maushold FollowMe/Feint FriendGuard; Tauros-Aqua Intimidate/CloseCombat. Plan: Gengar Mega Shadow Tag traps; Empoleon Fairy/Ice wall (fainted); Rotom-Mow Thunderbolt 2x Water; Grimmsnarl Prankster screens + Taunt; Slowbro Trick Room backup; Garchomp benched. Fake Out only works turn of switch-in.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Helping Hand boosts Blastoise-Mega's Ice Beam, which acts before Rotom-Mow and guarantees its KO from 46%. This removes the immediate Thunderbolt threat while preserving Politoed and avoids relying on Muddy Water's spread accuracy and weak damage.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott should be preserved for a later Prankster Tailwind or disruption turn, especially after Grimmsnarl is pressured or removed. Politoed remains valuable for re-establishing rain and providing Helping Hand or Icy Wind. Mega Blastoise is the preferred rain-mode attacker, while Choice Scarf Gholdengo remains useful into Grimmsnarl and Psychic-oriented teams.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Gengar)
decisions.rationale: Gengar must Protect: Politoed's rain-boosted spread Muddy Water would KO both my mons if Gengar doesn't block it (Gengar 15% < ~78 dmg). Grimmsnarl sets Light Screen since every foe attack is special. Preserve Gengar as my only damage dealer; accept Grimmsnarl's likely loss to the spread.
decisions.notebook: Opponent series team: Politoed (Drizzle rain; MuddyWater/IcyWind/HelpingHand/Protect; Calm), Whimsicott (Prankster Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast; FocusSash; Timid), Blastoise-Mega (Mega Launcher AuraSphere/WaterSpout/IceBeam/Protect; Modest), Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost ChoiceScarf MakeItRain/ShadowBall/Thunderbolt/Trick; Good as Gold blocks status; Modest), Maushold (FollowMe/Feint FriendGuard WideLens), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Intimidate CloseCombat/RagingBull/AquaJet). All foe attacks are special -> favor Light Screen. Gengar must Protect vs spread Muddy Water in rain. Plan: Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps; Grimmsnarl Prankster screens+Taunt; Rotom-Mow Thunderbolt 2x Water; Gengar Shadow Ball super-effective into Gholdengo (Ghost).

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Blastoise from Gengar’s faster attack while Politoed’s rain-boosted Muddy Water can KO both foes from their current HP. This keeps both Pokémon alive if successful and avoids sacrificing Blastoise for only Gengar.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Whimsicott for a later Prankster Tailwind or disruption turn, particularly once Grimmsnarl is pressured or removed. Politoed is valuable for restoring rain and providing Helping Hand or Icy Wind. Mega Blastoise is the preferred rain-mode attacker; Scarf Gholdengo remains useful into Grimmsnarl and Psychic-oriented teams.

decisions.rationale: Gengar is my last mon at 15% vs 4 foes; game is lost. Shadow Ball guarantees KO on Blastoise-Mega (3% HP) and Gengar's 178 Spe outspeeds it (98-130), landing the KO first. Mega Evolving drops Speed to 130 with no benefit (Shadow Tag can't save a 15% mon). Grimmsnarl is fainted, so slot 2 passes. Take the free KO.
decisions.notebook: Opponent series team: Politoed (Drizzle rain; MuddyWater/IcyWind/HelpingHand/Protect; Calm), Whimsicott (Prankster Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast; FocusSash; Timid), Blastoise-Mega (Mega Launcher AuraSphere/WaterSpout/IceBeam/Protect; Modest), Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost ChoiceScarf MakeItRain/ShadowBall/Thunderbolt/Trick; Good as Gold blocks status; Modest), Maushold (FollowMe/Feint FriendGuard WideLens), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Intimidate CloseCombat/RagingBull/AquaJet). All foe attacks special -> favor Light Screen. Gengar must Protect vs spread Muddy Water in rain. Shadow Ball IS super-effective (2x) vs Gholdengo (Ghost 2x x Steel 1x). Plan: Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps; Grimmsnarl Prankster screens+Taunt; Rotom-Mow Thunderbolt 2x Water. Game 1 likely lost (Gengar only survivor at 15%).

decisions.rationale: Politoed uses Icy Wind to damage Gengar and reduce its Speed, while Blastoise protects from Gengar’s faster attack. This preserves the 4% Blastoise and enables a likely Ice Beam finish next turn.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Whimsicott for a later Prankster Tailwind or disruption turn. Politoed is valuable for rain restoration, Helping Hand, and Icy Wind support. Mega Blastoise is the preferred rain-mode attacker; Scarf Gholdengo remains useful into Grimmsnarl and Psychic-oriented teams.

decisions.rationale: Pass with Politoed and bring in Scarf Gholdengo. Gengar is at 2% HP and heavily speed-dropped; Gholdengo can immediately finish it, while preserving Whimsicott for later Prankster Tailwind or disruption.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Whimsicott as a late-game Prankster support option, especially for Tailwind, Taunt, or Encore. Politoed remains valuable for rain restoration, Helping Hand, and Icy Wind support. Scarf Gholdengo is the preferred immediate cleaner and remains useful against Psychic-oriented teams and frail targets.

decisions.rationale: Game is unwinnable: only Gengar remains at 2% HP versus Politoed (68%), Gholdengo (83%), and benched Whimsicott. Any hit KOs Gengar; even Protect stalls only until PP runs out and Shadow Tag cannot secure a win. Forfeiting a mathematically lost game preserves focus for games 2-3 with zero series-cost downside.
decisions.notebook: Opponent series team: Politoed (Drizzle rain; MuddyWater/IcyWind/HelpingHand/Protect; Calm), Whimsicott (Prankster Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast; FocusSash; Timid), Blastoise-Mega (Mega Launcher AuraSphere/WaterSpout/IceBeam/Protect; Modest), Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost ChoiceScarf MakeItRain/ShadowBall/Thunderbolt/Trick; Good as Gold blocks status; Modest), Maushold (FollowMe/Feint FriendGuard WideLens), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Intimidate CloseCombat/RagingBull/AquaJet). All foe attacks special -> favor Light Screen. Gengar Shadow Ball 2x vs Gholdengo (Ghost). Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps. Game 1 lost: rain + spread special damage overwhelmed; Grimmsnarl fainted early, Rotom/Empoleon down. For game 2: lead Grimmsnarl screens + Gengar; Taunt Gholdengo turn 1 to deny Make It Rain; beware Whimsicott Tailwind speed flip and Politoed Icy Wind speed drops; keep Gengar healthy via Protect vs Muddy Water.

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Politoed while Scarf Gholdengo’s Shadow Ball moves before Gengar and should remove its remaining HP; if Gengar protects, Politoed avoids its follow-up and Gholdengo remains positioned to finish it next turn.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott remains a valuable late-game Prankster support option, especially for Tailwind, Taunt, and Encore. Politoed is useful for rain restoration, Helping Hand, and Icy Wind support. Scarf Gholdengo is the preferred immediate cleaner and remains valuable against Psychic-oriented teams and frail targets.

reflections.summary: Opponent's rain-boosted special spread (Blastoise Aura Sphere/Water Spout, Gholdengo Make It Rain, Politoed Icy Wind) overwhelmed us; we led Empoleon+Grimmsnarl, wasted Fake Out on status-immune Gholdengo, set screens too late, and never Mega Evolved Gengar to trap threats, leaving only 2% Gengar.
reflections.adjustment: Next game lead Grimmsnarl + Gengar and Mega Evolve Gengar turn 1 to Shadow Tag Gholdengo/Whimsicott and fire Shadow Ball, while Grimmsnarl uses Light Screen immediately instead of Fake Out.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tends to lead Mega Blastoise + Gholdengo (Good as Gold blocks status, immune to Taunt/Fake Out); Whimsicott & Politoed in back. Politoed mid-game sets Drizzle rain, uses Icy Wind speed control + Helping Hand. All foe attacks special -> Light Screen vital. Gengar Shadow Ball 2x vs Gholdengo; Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps. Game1 lost: no early screen, no Mega, Empoleon lead weak. Plan: lead Grimmsnarl Light Screen + Mega Gengar turn1; avoid status on Gholdengo; pressure Gholdengo with Gengar; beware Whimsicott Tailwind and Politoed Icy Wind.

reflections.summary: Won through strong matchup targeting: Gholdengo negated Fake Out, while Mega Blastoise and Politoed removed Empoleon and Rotom-Mow with Aura Sphere, Ice Beam, and Icy Wind. The four brought were suitable overall, but Mega Blastoise was exposed to both Rotom-Mow's Thunderbolt and Gengar's Shadow Ball.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the four, but plan Whimsicott/Gholdengo as the lead and preserve Mega Blastoise for a safer opening; switch it away immediately when Rotom-Mow can target it with Thunderbolt rather than accepting the trade.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's Grimmsnarl favors Prankster Fake Out, Taunt, and Light Screen support. Rotom-Mow applies major Electric pressure with Thunderbolt, while Gengar uses Protect and Shadow Ball to punish exposed targets. Prioritize denying Rotom-Mow free attacks and preserve Mega Blastoise until its Aura Sphere or Ice Beam targets are safe. Gholdengo's Fake Out immunity remains especially valuable into this structure. Whimsicott and Politoed remain useful for speed control and disruption.
